title: Fixed Size Array - Operator overloading basics
description:
---
_You probably noticed you could use `[]` on `std::vector`._ How you do stuff like this in C++ is called _operator overloads_. A operator overload is a method that is automatically called when you use a operator on a class, but some operator overloads are a bit weird. The common operator overload signature for binary operators is `T operator<operator>(const T& other);`, which returns the value, and takes the right hand side. This signature is the same for **+**, **-**, **/**, **\***, and **%**, so operator+ would be `T operator+(const T& other);`. The common comparison operators sig look like this: `bool operator<operator>(const T& rhs);` (same for ==, !=, >, <, etc.)
`operator=` is a bit strange. It typically is `<thisclass>& operator=(T other)`. The <thisclass>& return is for chaining so a = b = c, and other is obvious. The final operator for this lesson is `operator[]`, which typically has 2 signatures: `T& operator[](size_t index);` (mutible access, for assignment. T& will be changed by assignment, eg `obj[1] = val`), and `const T& operator[](size_t index) const;` for constant access (used when the object is const, return is usually reference, not a copy).
